issues_for_namespace.title: nginx container exits immediately because /etc/nginx/conf.d/site.conf is missing
issues_for_namespace.root_cause: The container's nginx configuration references /etc/nginx/conf.d/site.conf, which does not exist in the image, so nginx fails to start and exits with code 1 on every attempt.
issues_for_namespace.explanation: crashloop-nginx is in CrashLoopBackOff with ready 0/1, 3 restarts, and last exit code 1. The container log shows `nginx: [emerg] open() "/etc/nginx/conf.d/site.conf" failed (2: No such file or directory)`, and a Warning event reports repeated "Back-off restarting failed container nginx." CrashLoopBackOff is the symptom; the missing config file is the cause.
evidence: Pod crashloop-nginx status CrashLoopBackOff, ready 0/1, restarts 3, last exit code 1, reason Error
Container log: nginx: [emerg] open() "/etc/nginx/conf.d/site.conf" failed (2: No such file or directory)
Warning event: Back-off restarting failed container nginx in pod crashloop-nginx (count 3)
issues_for_namespace.fix: Provide /etc/nginx/conf.d/site.conf in the container (rebuild the image with the file, or mount a ConfigMap at that path) and ensure nginx.conf references an existing file, then roll out the corrected pod template and recreate the pod. Container image and volume mounts are immutable on a running pod, so the template must be corrected and the pod recreated (or the owning Deployment patched).
issues_for_namespace.prevention: Validate the nginx config with `nginx -t` in CI and require the config file to be present via a ConfigMap before deploying.
confidence_reasons: The log line directly names the missing file, and the pod state (CrashLoopBackOff, exit code 1, repeated restarts) agrees with a failing startup.

issues_for_namespace.title: Pod cannot start because image nginx:1.27-doesnotexist does not exist
issues_for_namespace.root_cause: The container image tag `nginx:1.27-doesnotexist` is not present in the container registry, so the kubelet cannot pull it and the pod stays in ImagePullBackOff.
issues_for_namespace.explanation: imagepull-nginx is Pending with reason ImagePullBackOff and 0 restarts (never started). The container waiting message and a FailedPull Warning event both state the image `docker.io/library/nginx:1.27-doesnotexist` is not found. This directly explains why the pod cannot run.
evidence: Pod imagepull-nginx status ImagePullBackOff, phase Pending, ready 0/1, restarts 0
Container message: failed to resolve reference "docker.io/library/nginx:1.27-doesnotexist": not found
Warning event: Failed to pull image "nginx:1.27-doesnotexist": ... not found (count 8)
issues_for_namespace.fix: Change the container image to a valid tag that exists in the registry (confirm the tag first, e.g. `nginx:1.27` or `nginx:stable`), then redeploy the pod from the corrected template. The image field is immutable on a running pod, so the pod must be recreated with the corrected image.
issues_for_namespace.prevention: Enforce image-tag validation in CI (reject unknown or `latest` tags) and verify the image exists in the registry before deploying.
confidence_reasons: The pod message and Warning event state directly that the image reference is not found, and the pod state (ImagePullBackOff, never started) agrees.

issues_for_namespace.title: Pod cannot be scheduled because node affinity matches no node
issues_for_namespace.root_cause: The pod's node affinity/selector requires a node that does not exist in the cluster, so the scheduler finds 0/1 available nodes and the pod remains Pending.
issues_for_namespace.explanation: pending-nginx is Pending with the message `0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector`, and a FailedScheduling Warning event repeats the same. With only one node and no match, the pod can never be placed.
evidence: Pod pending-nginx status Pending, message: 0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector
Warning event: FailedScheduling for Pod/pending-nginx with the same node-affinity message (count 1)
issues_for_namespace.fix: Remove or relax the pod's nodeAffinity/nodeSelector so it matches the existing node, or add a node with the required labels, then redeploy the pod. The affinity/selector is part of the immutable pod template, so correct the manifest and redeploy rather than editing the running pod.
kubectl_commands: kubectl -n ai-agent-failure-test get pod pending-nginx -o yaml
issues_for_namespace.prevention: Validate node affinity/selectors against actual node labels in CI or with a policy engine (e.g., Kyverno/OPA) before admitting pods.
confidence_reasons: The pod message and FailedScheduling event state directly that no node matches the affinity/selector, and the pod remains Pending (unscheduled).
